findings.title: p8_001 drops legacy report tables; downgrade destroys all P8 data
findings.why_it_matters: Two of the four dropped tables (`report_definitions`, `report_execution_logs`) genuinely exist in the bootstrap revision `dd47298c9c38_v3_1_full_schema_53_tables_adr_0023.py` (lines 474 and 1117) with a different legacy schema (`report_id` / `exec_id` / `template_id`, plus an FK from `report_definitions` to `template_files`). The migration's safety argument is a docstring assertion ("0 行"), not something the code checks — `op.drop_table(..., if_exists=True)` deletes whatever is there on whatever database it is pointed at, including any other developer's or a restored backup's copy that does have rows. There is no guard, no snapshot, and no post-drop verification, so a wrong premise is indistinguishable from a correct one after the fact. The `downgrade()` is symmetrically destructive: rolling back even one revision destroys every `report_files` row, which is an audit/product artifact (documented in `app/models/report.py` as an audit table that must not have rows deleted).
evidence: pcs-backend/alembic/versions/p8_001_report_tables.py:138-139 — downgrade: `    for t in _DROP_ORDER:` / `        op.drop_table(t, if_exists=True)`
pcs-backend/alembic/versions/p8_001_report_tables.py:3-7 — "但那两张表**从未被使用**（无 service / API / 前端引用，0 行）" — the 0-row premise is asserted in prose, not verified in code

findings.title: Nullable project_id defeats both unique constraints in Postgres
findings.why_it_matters: Both new unique constraints include `project_id`, which is deliberately nullable (`report_definitions.project_id` nullable=True at line 95-96, `report_styles.project_id` nullable=True at line 47-48 — both are company-level scope). PostgreSQL treats NULL as distinct from every other NULL in a unique index, so for company-level rows the constraint enforces nothing: two company-scope definitions with the same `name`, or two company-scope styles with the same `report_type` + `version`, both insert successfully. The only thing preventing duplicates today is an application-level check — `definition_service._reject_duplicate` (app/services/report/definition_service.py:317-327) and `style_service.create`'s `_current` probe (app/services/report/style_service.py:122-125) — and both are check-then-insert with no surrounding lock or `ON CONFLICT`, so two concurrent requests interleave and both pass. The result is two ACTIVE company-level styles at the same version, at which point `build_style`'s scoping becomes order-dependent and reports stop being reproducible against a frozen `style_version`. This is exactly the shape that stays green in tests (SQLite is not being asked to enforce it either) and only shows up on the real database under concurrency.
evidence: pcs-backend/app/services/report/definition_service.py:320-321 — `            ReportDefinition.project_id == project_id,` (application-level check-then-insert, no ON CONFLICT)
pcs-backend/app/services/report/style_service.py:122 — `        if await self._current(report_type, project_id) is not None:` (same TOCTOU shape)
findings.suggested_fix:
Make the DB enforce what the columns are actually claiming to enforce. The repo runs PostgreSQL 18 (CLAUDE.md), and `NULLS NOT DISTINCT` has been available since PG 15, so the minimal change is a dialect option on both constraints in p8_001 and their mirrors in `app/models/report.py`:

```python
sa.UniqueConstraint(
    "project_id", "name", name="uq_report_definitions_project_name",
    postgresql_nulls_not_distinct=True,
),
```

and the same on `uq_report_styles_scope_version` (ORM: `UniqueConstraint(..., postgresql_nulls_not_distinct=True)` inside each `__table_args__`). **Assumption I am naming rather than verifying:** `tests/conftest.py` builds the schema from ORM metadata against SQLite via `SA_Base.metadata.create_all`, and `postgresql_nulls_not_distinct` is a PostgreSQL dialect option — SQLAlchemy stores it as a dialect kwarg and skips it when compiling for another dialect, but this must be confirmed by running the suite, since SQLite's own unique-constraint semantics are unchanged either way (SQLite does treat NULLs as distinct, so the test DB will not enforce it — the guard under test belongs at the service layer regardless).

If you would rather not take the dialect option, the equivalent that works on both engines is two partial unique indexes plus a `COALESCE` sentinel column; that is a larger change and I would not recommend it before the NULLS NOT DISTINCT route is tried. Verification SQL after the change:

```sql
-- both should now raise unique_violation for a company-level (project_id IS NULL) duplicate
INSERT INTO report_definitions (def_id, project_id, name, category, description,
    definition_json, output_format, max_rows, version, status, shared_with)
VALUES (gen_random_uuid(), NULL, 'dup-probe', 'MANAGEMENT', '', '{}'::jsonb, 'pdf', 10, '0.1.0', 'DRAFT', 'ALL_USERS');
```

residual_risks: `report_files.content_hash` carries a GLOBAL unique constraint (`uq_report_files_content_hash`, p8_001:86) while the table carries a per-project `project_id`. `_upsert_report_file` (app/services/report/report_service.py:428-434) matches on `content_hash` alone and, on a hit, returns the existing row *without* rewriting `project_id`. Two projects that produce byte-identical canonical content therefore share one row whose `project_id` belongs to whichever project rendered first, and the second project will not see that file in a project-scoped listing. This is a schema-scope consequence rather than a migration bug, and I cannot tell from the diff whether cross-project content reuse is intended — flagging for a decision rather than a fix.

`report_definitions.def_id` is FK'd `ondelete="CASCADE"` from `report_execution_logs` (p8_001:119-120), while `report_files` intentionally carries no FK at all. Deleting a project therefore cascades away the execution audit trail but leaves the generated files (and their disk contents) behind. The model docstring at app/models/report.py:88-91 explains the missing FK on `report_files` as deliberate, but the two lifecycles diverging is worth an explicit decision.

p8_007's backfill maps every row with `report_file_id IS NULL` to `QUEUED`. Rows that had genuinely already FAILED before the `status` column existed are indistinguishable from rows that were still queued, so they are labelled `QUEUED` and then picked up by `reclaim_stale_execution_logs`, which rewrites `condition_snapshot` with a `reclaim_reason` of "worker 未完成". The end state (FAILED) is correct; the recorded reason is not what actually happened. Self-healing, but the audit line is misleading.

`p8_002`..`p8_007` use raw `op.execute` DDL rather than `op.add_column`. That is what buys the idempotency (`ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS`), but it also means those columns bypass Alembic's type/nullability inference — the ORM in app/models/report.py and the migration text must be kept in sync by hand, which is precisely the drift mode CLAUDE.md records. I verified the six added columns by eye (VARCHAR(50)/(20)/(64)/(16), UUID, DOUBLE PRECISION, INTEGER all match the ORM's String/Uuid/Float/Integer lengths) and they do match; that verification is manual and will not be re-run automatically.
testing_gaps: No test asserts the p8_007 backfill. A test that seeds `report_execution_logs` with one row having `report_file_id` set and one with it NULL, runs the migration's UPDATE statement, and asserts FINISHED/QUEUED respectively would pin the CASE mapping. Today the mapping is verified only by reading the SQL.

No test covers `p8_007`'s partial-run path — the exact scenario its own comment calls out ("已经跑过旧版这条迁移的库（开发库就是）"). Since the tests build schema from ORM metadata (tests/conftest.py, `SA_Base.metadata.create_all`) rather than from alembic revisions, no migration in this phase is exercised end-to-end by the suite at all.

No concurrency test for the two nullable-project_id unique constraints. A test that fires two concurrent company-scope style creates with the same `report_type` and asserts exactly one succeeds would fail today against PostgreSQL and pass silently against SQLite — which is the drift-blind-spot pattern CLAUDE.md warns about.

`p8_001`'s drop-then-create is not exercised anywhere: there is no test asserting that the legacy `report_definitions`/`report_execution_logs` are empty before the drop, so the '0 行' premise the migration's safety rests on is unverified by anything in the repo.
